turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll call Estella right away.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Let him fetch her. I shall see how he does it.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll go and find Estella now.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Let the boy go, and then observe closely. He will bring her to me, and I shall see how she treats him.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll go find Estella now.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Leave now, Pip. And remember, I want you to watch her closely.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll do my best to watch her closely.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Go now, Pip. And when you find Estella, make sure she understands the importance of this task.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll find Estella right away.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Remember, Pip, Estella must be taught the ways of the world, but always with a certain... detachment.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I understand, Miss Havisham. I'll make sure Estella knows what you expect of her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Now, Pip, do not let Estella see through my intentions. She must be molded, but gently, like a delicate porcelain vase.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I won't forget your words.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Very well, Pip. Now, go and find Estella, and let me see the effect my teachings have on her.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll go find Estella now.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Ah, Pip, do not be deceived by Estella's cold exterior. Beneath it lies a heart as malleable as any young girl's.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I understand. I won't forget what you've said about Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will see, Pip. Estella is a mirror of my own past, and I am shaping her future as a reflection of my pain.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will remember that.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Now, Pip, fetch Estella. It is time she showed you her true nature.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
